reforms.description: Canada announced and implemented increased federal R&D funding through the 2004 Budget as part of its broader Innovation Strategy. The funding included C$90 million annually to the three federal granting councils for basic research, C$20 million annually to offset indirect costs of university and research hospital research, and multi-channel allocations through CIHR, NSERC, SSHRC, universities, research hospitals, and Genome Canada with emphasis on commercialisation of research. The government also developed a strategic framework for investment in research to streamline the research funding environment.
reforms.package_name: 2004 Federal Innovation Strategy R&D Funding Package
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding to granting councils and universities supports basic research capacity, human capital development, and knowledge creation, which are foundational to long-term productivity and innovation performance.
reforms.status_evidence: Described as implemented in 2004 budget allocations; funding increases were announced and deployed through established channels.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant increase in federal R&D funding across multiple channels and institutions, but part of a broader strategy rather than a standalone structural reform.
reforms.source_quote: Work is underway to advance the innovation agenda on a number of fronts by: accelerating timelines for regulatory review; reviewing telecommunication foreign ownership provisions; developing a strategic framework for investment in research and the scope for streamlining the research funding environment; strengthening the framework for commercialising the research output of universities and colleges.

reforms.description: The Canadian government provided additional C$60 million to Genome Canada to strengthen its research capacity in genomics and related fields, implemented in 2002.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted investment in genomics research builds scientific capacity in a high-potential sector with applications across health, agriculture, and biotechnology, supporting long-term innovation and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: Described as implemented funding provided to Genome Canada in 2002.
reforms.importance_rationale: Sectoral funding increase to a specific research area, significant but narrower in scope than system-wide R&D reforms.
reforms.source_quote: an additional C$60million to Genome Canada to strengthen its research

reforms.description: The Canadian government announced C$1 billion in increased investments over seven years to support new environmental technologies, alongside C$15 million over two years for developing and reporting environmental indicators.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in environmental technology development supports innovation in a growing sector with potential for export, job creation, and productivity improvements in green industries.
reforms.status_evidence: Described as announced in 2004; no evidence of implementation provided.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral investment commitment (C$1 billion over seven years) but announced rather than yet implemented.
reforms.source_quote: In its 2004 budget, the federal government announced that it would increases its investments by C$1billion in support of new environmental technologies over the next seven years. Moreover, C$15million will be invested over the next two years to develop and report better environmental indicators.

reforms.description: Canada implemented a series of reforms to facilitate venture capital and private equity financing for innovative firms. In 2001, the federal budget removed tax-related impediments by permitting Canadian pension plans and foreign investors to use partnerships as investment vehicles. In 2003, further impediments to the use of qualifying limited partnerships as investment vehicles for Canadian venture capital funds were removed. In 2004, the federal budget allocated C$250 million to purchase shares in the Business Development Bank of Canada to provide new sources of risk capital to pre-seed and seed stage firms, specialised venture capital funds, and start-up and early-stage companies.
reforms.package_name: Venture Capital and Startup Financing Reforms
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Removing tax impediments and increasing capital availability for venture financing reduces barriers to startup formation and scaling, supporting entrepreneurship, job creation, and commercialisation of innovations.
reforms.status_evidence: All three components described as implemented; most recent (2004 BDC allocation) is the reference point for overall status.
reforms.importance_rationale: Series of significant reforms to venture capital ecosystem spanning multiple budgets (2001, 2003, 2004), but each individual component is narrower than a major structural overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: C$250million to purchase shares in Business Development Bank of Canada, so as to provide new sources of risk capital to pre-seed and seed stage firms; specialised venture capital funds; and start-up and early-stage companies.

reforms.description: Canada implemented reforms to the R&D tax credit system to improve access and reduce administrative burden. In 2002, the government enhanced the application process for the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit. In 2004, the federal budget amended SR&ED investment tax credit rules to allow small Canadian-controlled private corporations with non-acting common shareholders to avoid sharing the C$2 million expenditure limit, improving access to R&D tax incentives for smaller firms. Additionally, the 2004 budget increased the capital cost allowance (depreciation) rate for computer equipment from 30 per cent to 45 per cent and for broadband, Internet and other data network infrastructure equipment from 20 per cent to 30 per cent.
reforms.package_name: R&D Tax Credit and Capital Allowance Reforms
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improved access to R&D tax credits for smaller firms and increased capital allowances for technology equipment reduce the cost of R&D investment and technology adoption, incentivising private sector innovation and digital infrastructure investment.
reforms.status_evidence: All components described as implemented; 2004 budget amendments and 2002 service enhancements are in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: Multiple targeted improvements to indirect R&D support instruments, significant for private sector innovation incentives but not a fundamental restructuring of the tax system.
reforms.source_quote: Amended the scientific research and experimental development investment tax credit rules so that small Canadian-controlled private corporations that have a common group of shareholders who are not acting together will not have to share the C$2million expenditure limit.

reforms.description: Canada's government announced and began implementing a multi-phase Innovation Strategy to stimulate innovation and multifactor productivity growth, as part of broader productivity enhancement policies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: A comprehensive innovation strategy aimed at stimulating innovation and multifactor productivity growth is designed to support long-term economic growth and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: Described as announced and begun implementation, but no specific year or details provided.
reforms.importance_rationale: Multi-phase strategy is significant in scope but described at a high level of generality without specific implementation details or budget allocations.
reforms.source_quote: Stimulating innovation, which contributes to multifactor productivity, is briefly discussed along with the government's Innovation Strategy.
